en: The Great Cloud Wheel Sutra for Invoking Rain, Volume One, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas during the Sui Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying in the palace of the nāga kings Nanda and Upananda.
Within,
he dwelt in the midst of the great cloud-wheel palace and precious tower, which was a treasury of mani-jewels of great majesty,
surrounded on all sides by a great assembly of bhikṣus and bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable great dragon kings,
their names being Nanda Dragon King and Upananda Dragon King.
The Naga King Sagara,
the Naga King Anavatapta,
and the Naga King Manasvin.
The Naga King Varuṇa,
the Naga King Takṣaka,
and the Naga King Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

and the Dragon King Maṇiratna-śikhin.
The Naga King Radiant Crown,

The Dragon King Śakra-dhara,

Sūryaprabha Dragon King,

Ratnaśikhara Dragon King,

The Naga King Sumeruṇa,

The Naga King Bhīṣaṇa,
the Naga King Suśrī,

The Naga King Balira,
the Naga King Mīyaca,

The nāga kings Bhīṣma, Jvālana,
and Saptasīrṣa.
The Dragon King Mahākāya,

The Naga King Great Banner of Marks,

The Naga King Tejorāśigarbha,

and the Naga King Rātridhara.
The Dragon King Varṣa,
the Dragon King Megha-varṣa,
and the Dragon King Mahā-megha-varṣa.
The Dragon King Fire-Light,
the Dragon King Great Cloud Lord,
and the Dragon King Free from Anger.
The Nāga King Kukuṇḍa,
the Nāga King Nāgaśūra,
and the Nāga King Śaṅkhinī.
The Nāga King Meghāvara,
the Nāga King Airāvaṇa,
and the Nāga King Tejodhipati.
The Dragon King of Clouds,
the Dragon King of Infinite Steps,
and the Dragon King of Sublime Features.
The Great-Body Nāga King,
the Large-Belly Nāga King,
and the Well-Examined Nāga King.
The nāga kings Pangu, Gopana, and Uttara.
The Dragon King Fierce Poison,
the Dragon King Wondrous Sound,
and the Dragon King Ambrosial Reality.
The Dragon King Great Shower,
the Dragon King Muffled Sound,
and the Dragon King Thunderclap.
The Dragon King Drum-Shaking Sound,
the Dragon King Showering Nectar,

The Nāga King Vajrasvara,
the Nāga King Śūradhara,
and the Nāga King Nārāyaṇa.
The Nāga King Śuṣkoda and the Nāga King Vikaṭa were the leaders among such great nāga kings;
furthermore, there were eighty-four billion nayutas of other nāga kings.
They all came together to that assembly.
Then, all those dragon kings rose from their seats,
adjusted their robes, and bared their right shoulders.
Kneeling with his right knee on the ground and joining his palms toward the Buddha,
he immediately offered various kinds of immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable numbers of exquisite flowers,
scented pastes, and powdered incense.
Flower crowns, garments, precious banners, pennants, and canopies;
dragon-flower jeweled crowns, pearl necklaces,
precious flowers, silken ribbons, and pearl lattices.
They draped various jeweled pendants and tassels over the Tathāgata,
performed various musical entertainments, clapped their hands, and sang praises,
giving rise to a heart of profound reverence and extraordinary wonder.
Having circumambulated them hundreds of thousands of times, they withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, once all the nāgas were stationed to one side, they all made this vow:
"May we, by means of oceans of bodies as numerous as the atoms within all the oceans of worlds..."
The ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas pervade all oceans of worlds,
having already transcended all oceans of atoms of earth, water, fire, and wind.
All the oceans of the number of atoms in all forms and radiances,
which have already surpassed immeasurable, inconceivable,
and ineffable *asaṃkhyeya* numbers of oceans of various bodies.
From each and every body, they emanate immeasurable oceans of clouds of hands, as numerous as asaṃkhyeyas, pervading the ten directions. Furthermore,
from within each and every minute particle,
they manifest immeasurable oceans of clouds of offerings, pervading the ten directions.
This shall be used to make offerings to the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, continuing without interruption.
Thus it is immeasurable, inconceivable, and ineffable.
An incalculable number of Samantabhadra Bodhisattvas’ clouds of oceans of bodies fill the entirety of space,
abiding and sustaining themselves without interruption.
Such are the clouds of oceans of bodies of these bodhisattvas.

That is to say: clouds of oceans of all wheel-marks; clouds of oceans of all jeweled crowns; clouds of oceans of great luminous jewel-treasury carriages; clouds of oceans of all powdered-incense-tree treasuries; clouds of oceans of all incense-smoke manifesting various colors; clouds of oceans of all musical sounds; clouds of oceans of all fragrant trees—and such as these, immeasurable and boundless.
Inconceivable, ineffable, and numbering in incalculable *asaṃkhyeya*s;
such oceans of clouds of offerings as these fill the entirety of space, remaining and persisting without interruption.
They made offerings, paid homage, revered, and prostrated before the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, they produced clouds of oceans of mani-jewel kings from the lightning-treasury of all adorned realms,
and clouds of oceans of mani-jewel kings adorned with universally radiant jewel-rain.
Clouds of oceans of maṇi-jewel kings with the radiance of all jewels, harmonizing with the Buddha’s voice;
clouds of oceans of maṇi-jewels whose sounds of all Buddha-dharmas pervade everywhere;
clouds of oceans of light from the transformations of all Buddhas, consisting of jewel-flames from all universal gates.
Clouds of mani-jewel kings of the ocean of all radiant ornaments appearing without interruption;
clouds of mani-jewel kings of the ocean of all light-flames that accord with the holy conduct of the Buddhas;
clouds of mani-jewel kings of the ocean of lightning-light from the inconceivable buddha-fields of the Tathāgatas.
The radiant colors of all exquisite jewels— the bodies of the Buddhas of the three periods of time,
oceans of maṇi-jewel kings, clouds of such things, and the luminous hues of all these various gems—
pervade and fill the void, abiding and sustaining themselves without interruption.
They offer worship, reverence, respect, and prostrations to the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

Furthermore, there issued forth ocean-like clouds of all indestructible, wondrous jewel incense and flower chariots; ocean-like clouds of chariots adorned with all boundless-colored mani-jewel kings; ocean-like clouds of chariots with the light-flames of all jewel lamps and incense; ocean-like clouds of chariots of all pearl-like exquisite colors; ocean-like clouds of chariots with all flower pedestals; ocean-like clouds of chariots adorned with all jewel crowns; ocean-like clouds of treasure-trove chariots whose adornments of light-flames pervading all ten directions were unceasing; ocean-like clouds of chariots adorned with all boundlessly manifesting supreme jewels; ocean-like clouds of chariots with all-pervasive, exquisite adornments; and ocean-like clouds of chariots with nets of flower-bells on all doors and railings—such as these, filling the entirety of space, remained and continued without end.
They made offerings, paid homage, and prostrated before the ocean-like clouds of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, they brought forth ocean-like clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of exquisite golden jewel necklaces,
and ocean-like clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of the brilliant colors of all flowers.
Ocean-clouds of lion thrones of the lotus-treasury of all dark-blue maṇi-jāmbūnada-gold-colored lotuses;
ocean-clouds of lion thrones of the lotus-treasury of all maṇi-lamps;
ocean-clouds of lion thrones of the lotus-treasury of fire-colored exquisite flowers from all maṇi-jewel banners.
The ocean-clouds of lion-thrones within the lotus-treasury of wondrous colors adorned with all kinds of jewels;
the ocean-clouds of lion-thrones within the lotus-light treasury of Indra, delightful for all to behold;
and the ocean-clouds of lion-thrones within the lotus-treasury of inexhaustible flaming light, delightful for all to behold.
The ocean-clouds of lion thrones of the Lotus Treasury Universally Illumined by All Jewel Radiance,
and the ocean-clouds of lion thrones of the Lotus Light Treasury of the Voices of All Buddhas—
such as these, filling all of space, remained present and uninterrupted.
I offer worship, respect, and prostrations to the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

Furthermore, there appeared clouds of oceans of *maṇi* trees emitting all manner of wondrous sounds; clouds of oceans of trees whose leaves, joined together on all sides like palms, emitted fragrant scents; clouds of oceans of trees manifesting infinite radiant colors through every adornment; clouds of oceans of jewel-trees from which issued clouds of all flowers; clouds of oceans of trees that produce an infinite treasury of adornments; clouds of oceans of trees with jewel wheels blazing like lightning; clouds of oceans of trees manifesting the upper halves of Bodhisattvas’ bodies emerging from sandalwood powder; clouds of oceans of trees adorning the Bodhimanda with inconceivable and boundless tree deities; clouds of oceans of trees with the sun’s radiance appearing from a treasury of precious robes; and clouds of oceans of trees, delightful to behold, from which everywhere issued truly wondrous sounds. All such [clouds] filled the void, remaining and supporting one another without ceasing.
They made offerings of worship, reverence, respect, and prostration to the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, they produced ocean-clouds of lion-thrones from the treasury of infinite jewel-colored lotuses,
and ocean-clouds of lion-thrones from the electric treasury of universal-magnificent mani-kings, surrounding them on all sides.
Ocean-clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of all ornaments and adornments;
ocean-clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of the blazing flames of lamps of all exquisite jewel crowns;
ocean-clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of the rain of jewels issuing from perfect sounds.
Ocean-clouds of lion-thrones from the treasury of all flower-crowns, incense-flowers, and jewels, upon which all Buddhas sit, manifesting adornments;
ocean-clouds of lion-thrones from the treasury of mani-jewel kings, adorned with all kinds of railings and hanging garlands;
ocean-clouds of lion-thrones from the treasury of adornments.
Oceans of clouds of lion thrones from the treasuries of fragrant tips of the branches and leaves of all mani-jewel trees;
oceans of clouds of lion thrones from the sun-light treasury, universally adorned with nets of exquisite fragrant jewel bells—
such as these fill the entirety of space, remaining and sustaining themselves without interruption.
They made offerings of worship, reverence, respect, and prostration to the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, they produced ocean-clouds of canopies of all kinds of wish-fulfilling *maṇi* jewel-kings,
and ocean-clouds of canopies adorned with various flowers upon pedestals of *indra-nīla* jewels.
Ocean-clouds of canopies of all fragrant mani-jewels;
ocean-clouds of canopies with the appearance of flames from all jewel lamps;
ocean-clouds of canopies of sovereign mani-jewel kings that produce sounds through the spiritual power of all Buddhas.
Oceans of clouds of canopies adorned with the light of all manifest mani-jewel robes;
oceans of clouds of jewel canopies of all flower-light flames;
oceans of clouds of canopies filled everywhere with the sounds of exquisite bells from all nets.
Ocean-clouds of canopies of lotus nets and pedestals of inexhaustible, wondrously colored mani-jewels;
ocean-clouds of canopies of flaming jewel banners and pedestals of all kinds of golden flowers;
ocean-clouds of canopies of inconceivable ornaments of various radiant necklaces.
In this manner, they pervade the entirety of space, remaining and sustaining themselves without interruption,
making offerings, paying homage, honoring, and prostrating before the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, there issued forth ocean-clouds of all kinds of exquisite mani-jewel canopies;
ocean-clouds of flower canopies adorned with all manner of infinite radiance;
and ocean-clouds of wondrous canopies containing pearls of boundless colors.
Cloud-oceans of the Mani-jewel King Canopies of the Sound of the Gate of Compassion of All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
cloud-oceans of all exquisite colored jewel-flame flower crowns and wonderful canopies;
cloud-oceans of wonderful canopies of jewel-luminous adornments with hanging bell nets.
Ocean-clouds of canopies of all kinds of mani-tree branch necklaces;
ocean-clouds of canopies of all sun-illumining, translucent-flame mani-kings and fragrant incense smoke;
ocean-clouds of canopies that universally perfume with treasuries of all sandalwood powder.
The entire expanse of space was filled with oceans of clouds of canopies, universally adorned with the lightning-flame brilliance of the ultimate realm of all Buddhas;
these remained and were maintained without interruption as offerings of worship,
reverence, respect, and prostration to the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, there emerged clouds of oceans of all-jeweled bright wheels,
clouds of oceans of all-jeweled flame-marked light wheels,
and clouds of oceans of all-flower-flame-light wheels.
Cloud-oceans of light-wheel circles of all Buddha-flower jewel radiance;
cloud-oceans of light-wheel circles appearing and entering all Buddha-fields;
cloud-oceans of jewel-branch light-wheels with the universal-gate sounds of the spheres of all Buddhas.
Cloud-oceans of flaming light-wheels of all vaidūrya-jewel-nature maṇi-kings;
cloud-oceans of color-form light-wheels manifested in a single thought-moment for all sentient beings;
and cloud-oceans of great thundering light-wheels of sounds that please all Buddhas.
With clouds of oceans of light-wheels from mani-jewel kings of wondrous sound for all the assemblies of sentient beings to be converted,
filling the entirety of space and remaining without interruption, they made offerings, paid homage, showed respect, and prostrated before the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

Furthermore, there emerged clouds of oceans of flames from the treasury of all *maṇi* jewels; clouds of oceans of flames of the colors, sounds, fragrances, tastes, and textures of all Buddhas; clouds of oceans of flames of all jewel-flames; clouds of oceans of flames of the thunderous sounds of all Buddha-dharmas pervading everywhere; clouds of oceans of flames of lightning-light from the adornments of all Buddha-fields; clouds of oceans of flames of light from all flower-litters; clouds of oceans of flames of light from all jewel-flutes; clouds of oceans of flames of the voices of Buddhas appearing throughout all eons to teach and transform sentient beings; clouds of oceans of flames manifesting inexhaustible jewel-flower garlands for sentient beings; and clouds of oceans of flames manifesting the adornments of all thrones—all such as these filled the void, remaining and supporting without end.

They made offerings, paid homage, revered, and prostrated before the ocean-like clouds of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Furthermore, they brought forth oceans of clouds of uninterrupted and unscattered light from jewels of infinite colors;

oceans of clouds of the universal radiance of all *maṇi* jewel-kings; oceans of clouds of lightning-light adorning all Buddha-fields; oceans of clouds of all fragrant lights; oceans of clouds of all adorned lights; oceans of clouds of the transformation-body lights of all Buddhas; oceans of clouds of the light of flower-garlands from all various jewel trees; oceans of clouds of the light of all garments; oceans of clouds of the light of the jewel-kings of the renown of all the boundless practices of Bodhisattvas; and oceans of clouds of the light of all pearl lamps. All such [clouds] filled the void, remaining and persisting without ceasing.
They made offerings of, paid homage to, revered, and prostrated before the ocean-like clouds of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, they brought forth ocean-like clouds of all kinds of inconceivable, diverse incense and flowers,
and ocean-like clouds of jewel-flame lotus flower nets.
Cloud-seas of light-orbs of all infinite and boundless colored mani-jewel kings;
cloud-seas of caskets containing all kinds of mani-jewels and pearl-colored treasures;
and cloud-seas of powdered sandalwood incense made of all kinds of exquisite mani-jewels.
Ocean-clouds of all mani-jewel canopies;
ocean-clouds of all pure and wondrous sounds that delight the hearts of all beings;
ocean-clouds of all jewel-kings and pearl necklaces with tassels like wheels of solar radiance.
With clouds of oceans of all boundless jewel treasuries and clouds of oceans of the physical bodies of all Samantabhadras,

and with all such [offerings] filling the entirety of space, they continuously abide in support of, and perform offerings, reverence, respect, and prostrations to the oceans of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
At that time, these eighty-four billion hundred thousand nayutas of dragon kings in the assembly, having made this vow, circumambulated the Buddha three times,
prostrated with their heads at his feet, and stood to one side.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the dragon kings, saying, "You dragon kings,
each of you should return to your seats.
When the dragon kings heard the Buddha's words, they did so.
Each returned to their respective places and sat down in order.
At that time, there was a dragon king within the assembly named Anantavyūha-sāgaramegha-tejorāja-cakracchatra.
Among the dragon kings within this trichiliocosm,
he is the most preeminent and great; having attained non-retrogression,
he has assumed this dragon body through the power of his original vows.
Desiring to make offerings to, revere, and pay homage to the Tathāgata,
they have come to be born within this Jambudvīpa to hear and receive the True Dharma.
At that time, the Dragon King rose from his seat.
He adjusted his robes, bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha,
and spoke these words: "World-Honored One, I now have a doubt."
"I wish to question the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
If the Buddha would grant me permission, I would then venture to ask.
Having spoken these words, he remained silent.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Dragon King Anantavyūha-sāgara-megha-tejo-rāja-cakravarti-śrī-garbha, saying these words:
"O Great Dragon King, if you have any doubts, feel free to ask whatever you wish."
"I shall now analyze and explain this for you so as to bring you joy.
Having spoken these words,
at that time the Dragon King Anantavyūha-sāgara-megha-tejo-rāja-cakravarti-vitāna addressed [the Buddha].
He then addressed the Buddha, saying: "Indeed, World-Honored One,
how can you cause all the dragon kings to extinguish all suffering and obtain peace and happiness?"
Having experienced peace and happiness, he further causes sweet rain to fall in due season within this Jambudvīpa,
so that all trees, groves, medicinal herbs, and crops grow and all produce their essential flavors.
"May all people throughout Jambudvīpa receive every form of happiness.
When the World-Honored One heard these words,
he immediately addressed the Great Nāga King Anantavyūha-samudra-megha-tejo-rāja-cakravarti-śrī-garbha, saying:
Excellent, excellent!
It is for the sake of benefiting those sentient beings that you are now able to ask the Tathāgata about such matters as these.
"Listen attentively, Great Dragon King, listen attentively and reflect well upon this.
I shall analyze and explain it for you.
Wheel-Covered Dragon King, I possess a single dharma."
If you are able to practice this fully, it will cause all nāgas to eliminate all suffering and become endowed with perfect peace and happiness. What is this one dharma?
It is the practice of great loving-kindness (mahāmaitrī).
Great Dragon King, if there are gods or humans who practice great loving-kindness,
fire cannot burn them, water cannot drown them,
poison cannot harm them, and blades cannot wound them.
Neither internal nor external enemies or thieves can plunder them;
whether sleeping or awake, they always attain peace and security.
By the power of practicing great loving-kindness, they possess great majestic virtue.
The gods and the world cannot disturb them;
their physical appearance is upright and majestic, and they are loved and respected by all.
Wherever they go, they encounter no obstacles whatsoever.
All sufferings are extinguished and the mind attains joy;
because of the power of great compassion, all forms of happiness are fulfilled,
and after the end of life, one is reborn in the Brahma Heaven.
Great Dragon King, if there are gods or humans who practice great loving-kindness,
they shall obtain such immeasurable and boundless benefits as these.
Therefore, O Dragon King, you must always practice those deeds of great loving-kindness through your body, speech, and mind.
Furthermore, O Dragon Kings,
there is a dhāraṇī called "Bestowing Peace and Happiness upon All Sentient Beings.
You dragons must constantly recite it, maintain mindfulness of it, and uphold it.
They are able to extinguish all the suffering and afflictions of the nāgas and bestow upon them peace and happiness.
Once those nāgas have obtained such happiness,
they are finally able to send down sweet rain upon Jambudvīpa in accordance with the proper seasons.
He causes all trees, forests, medicinal herbs,
and crops to produce their essential flavors.
At that time, the Dragon King again addressed the Buddha, saying:
What is called the "dhāraṇī phrase for bestowing all happiness"?
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke the mantra as follows: *Tadyathā*.

Regarding these mantra syllables: those with a mark beside the mouth (the *jihvāmūlīya*) are to be read by curling the tongue; those marked with a *dīrgha* (long) vowel are to be drawn out with a prolonged sound.
Recite it: *dhāraṇī dhāraṇī* (1), *udāraṇī* (2), *āḥ* (3), *prajñe* (all *di-li* in reverse;
*śī-chi-chu-li* in reverse) (3), *vijaya-vardhana-satye-prajñe* (4), *prahāṇa-vardhana*.

In an age of famine and evil, when pestilence abounds and people act unlawfully and with disorder, the populace shall be filled with terror.

Furthermore, it can shatter and disperse all demons,

obstacles, and strange portents caused by malevolent stars.

The Venerable Nāgamātṛ, named Puṇḍarīka-mahāmegha-tejo-ratiprabha, the Honored Great Nāga King,
possesses a body that is cool and sustains a great wind-wheel through the power of the true practice of all Buddhas.
She rained down the rain of the six flavors and spoke this mantra:
*Gala gala* (1), *kili kili* (2), *kulu kulu* (3), *kirini kirini* (4), *kuma kuma kuma kuma kuma kuma kuma kuma kuma*—nine times *kuma* (5)—O Mother of the Nine-Headed Dragon!
An imperial decree addressed to those who wear the great cloud-lightning-flower crown as their foremost head-ornament;
who hold all dragons and wear cloud-garments;
who subdue the poisonous vapors of all realms and are adorned with clouds upon which they ride.
The thunder resounds afar, able to announce itself to all the nāgas, and they are surrounded by great clouds;
this is due to the power of the Buddhas' true practice,
which causes rain to be requested throughout the land of Jambudvīpa.
May a great rain descend and bring full sufficiency. Svāhā.

"By the true power of all Buddhas of the three periods of time,
and by the mind of compassion, svāhā. At that time,
having spoken this mantra, the World-Honored One addressed the Dragon King, saying:
If there is a drought and one wishes to invoke rain,
the presiding ritualist must necessarily give rise to a mind of compassion toward all sentient beings. Furthermore,
if there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs involved, their preceptual conduct must have been fundamentally pure from the outset.
If one has previously committed an offense of *niḥsargika-pāyattika* or even those of the *śaikṣa-dharmas*,
one must perform a solemn confession for seven days and seven nights prior;
if among laypeople, one must likewise do so for seven days and seven nights prior.
One must daily receive the Eightfold Precepts of the Fast,
and even on the day of performing the ritual for requesting rain,
one must remain entirely pure and free from indolence or arrogance.
One should prepare a site on a truly pure plot of open ground,
removing all gravel and thorny weeds.
A space of twelve paces should be established as the *maṇḍala* site, and within it, an altar of ten paces square should be raised.
The altar should be one chi high and smeared with the dung of a *gavya* cow;
take fresh, pure dung to plaster the perimeter of the altar.
In the center of the altar, arrange a high seat.
On the seat, spread a new, blue, clean mat and hang a new blue canopy.
Three cubits from the east side of the high seat,
use cow dung juice to draw a nāga king with one body and three heads.
One should also depict the dragon king’s retinue surrounding him on both sides.
Five cubits to the south of the high seat,
one should paint the dragon king with five heads upon a single body.
Furthermore, paint various nāgas surrounding [the central figure] on both the left and right.
Seven cubits to the west of the high seat,
paint a nāgarāja with one body and seven heads.
Furthermore, paint various nāgas surrounding [the central figure] on both the left and right.
Measuring nine cubits outward from the north side of the high seat,
depict a single-bodied, nine-headed nāga king.
Furthermore, paint various nāgas surrounding [the mandala] on the left and right.
At the four corners of the altar, place four flower vases, each with a capacity of three sheng.
Also, use refined gold or stone ink (shidai).
Add water to make it clear until the flask is completely full.
Insert various flowering trees and diverse flower stamens into the flask.
At each of the four gates of the *maṇḍala*, place a large, exquisite incense burner.
Burn various incenses, such as olibanum, liquid storax, bdellium, sandalwood, and安息 (An-xi, *An-hsi*) incense.
Hang seven blue banners at each of the four corners;
together there shall be twenty-eight banners, each one zhang in length.
Furthermore, ghee-oil lamps should be provided in a number corresponding to that of the banners.
Various fruits, ghee, curd, and milk porridge should be set out on all four sides.
Before the various dragon kings, one should scatter flowers and burn incense without interruption.
As for its fruits, food, and water from the jars,
these must be freshly prepared every day and may not remain overnight;
one should always provide the offerings at dawn, at the very moment the sun first rises.
Those who read this scripture shall bathe three times each day with fragrant water,
don new green robes, observe the fast, and contemplate in stillness;
they shall eat only ghee, curd, milk porridge, and so forth, along with non-glutinous rice, fruits, and vegetables.
If one must defecate or urinate, one must also bathe.
When ascending the high seat, one first pays homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions,
burns incense, scatters flowers, and respectfully invites all Buddhas of the ten directions and all great Bodhisattvas.
As well as all the devas and nāga kings;
for the sake of protecting the person reciting the mantra,
one may consecrate pure water or white ash with mantras.
One should bind the boundary by fixing the mind upon one's own heart,
whether over a single step or many steps,
using either water or ash as the demarcation.
Furthermore, one should consecrate a thread with mantras to form knots,
which are then tied upon the crown of the head and around the hands and feet.
When consecrating water, one should sprinkle it over the neck and upon the forehead.
One should form this thought:
those with evil minds shall not enter the boundary of this mandala.
The one who recites the mantra should always give rise to a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings and never harbor malicious thoughts.
Furthermore, I vow to dedicate these merits from my worship of the Buddha, my recitations,
and all other virtuous deeds to all devas and nāga kings,
as well as to all sentient beings and those with physical form.
When ascending the Dharma seat, one should recite this sutra and its dhāraṇī in a loud voice, without ceasing day or night.
Whether for seven days, or two weeks,
or at the latest three weeks, sweet rain will surely descend.
"Except for those who lack single-minded mindfulness, those who lack a heart of compassion, and those who are defiled and turbid.
The Buddha told the Dragon King:
"The tides of the ocean may still swell or recede."
These words are true, certain, and not false.
At that time, the dragon kings, having received the Buddha’s teaching,
leaped for joy and prostrated themselves in worshipful practice.
The Great Cloud Wheel Sutra on Invoking Rain, Scroll II.
